newsitem.title: USA: Arctic Cat sees higher garment sales for year.
newsitem.headline: Arctic Cat sees higher garment sales for year.

text.p: Arctic Cat Inc, which reported lower fiscal 1998 first quarter sales due to a shift in snowmobile garment shipments to the second quarter from the first, said Friday it expects garment sales for the full year to exceed last year's level.

"We executed a planned shift in shipments of snowmobile garments from the first quarter to the second quarter in order to link our supply more closely with dealer and consumer demand," said Christopher Twomey, president and chief executive officer, in a news release.

"The shift resulted in a temporary and predictable decrease in revenues. These shipments will be reflected in our second quarter revenues, and we fully expect garment sales in this fiscal year to exceed last year's levels," he said.

Earlier today, the company reported sales for its fiscal 1998 first quarter ended June 30, 1997 fell to $85.5 million from $89.1 million in the same period last year. Net earnings for the quarter declined to $872,000 or $0.03 a share from $1.0 million or $0.03 for the first quarter last year.

Arctic Cat said its operating expenses rose in its first quarter but it expects that, by the end of the year, they will be consistent with prior year's operating expenses, when calculated as a percent of sales.
Based on orders already received, Twomey also said the company continues to expect an increase in revenues and earnings for the fiscal year.
